# Chesed Brainstorm — Every Honest Voice Path

The Awtsmoos gives speech an ohr of meaning and a keli of waveform; Awtsmoos.com must not let either disappear when the movie crosses adapter, asset, decoder, mixer, and muxer shore.

## Possibilities
1. Preserve canonical speech metadata directly in `AnimatorMoviePlanParts.js`.
2. Extract dialogue projection into a dedicated module so speech semantics do not crowd the already-large plan-parts file.
3. Silence all missing voices explicitly; rejected because the acceptance film intentionally authors spoken dialogue.
4. Teach the mixer to synthesize speech dynamically; rejected for this proof because export should be deterministic and offline once assets exist.
5. Generate acceptance AIFF files with macOS `say`; promising because the target host already exposes stable installed voices and the mixer expects AIFF.
6. Generate WAV then convert to AIFF with ffmpeg; possible fallback if `say -o` produces an incompatible flavor.
7. Generate speech at server-render time; rejected because that would make ffmpeg bridge own semantic generation instead of encoding only witnessed assets.
8. Keep a source-controlled voice specification that maps each authored speaker to exact line text, voice name, rate, and expected filename.
9. Keep generated binaries as reproducible proof assets and record source generator/provenance.
10. Validate asset count and filenames against the projected dialogue before rendering.
11. Decode generated AIFFs through `AnimatorBrowserAiffDecoder` in browser runtime before accepting them.
12. Measure AIFF durations and ensure they fit line windows; if longer, choose rates deliberately instead of truncating silently.
13. Preserve `speakerName`, `voiceStatus`, `silentMode`, `emotion`, `voice`, `speechStyle`, and `rate` across the adapter so future renderers can use them.
14. Preserve `speakerId` and display mode for compatibility.
15. Avoid making `AnimatorBrowserVoiceAssets` infer missing speakers; adapter truth belongs upstream.
16. Add contract tests after the full source pass, not before.

## Ideal world
Every authored dialogue entity reaches Animator with its entire speech covenant intact. A reproducible generator materializes prepared voice assets from a declarative specification. Browser decoding proves bytes are valid. The production soundtrack schedules those voices at canonical edit times. Native ffmpeg then receives the already-rendered soundtrack without ever deciding what a character should say.
